correctness.rationale: Angular samples rescaled by n converge as a point process to stationary rate λ=1/(2π) Poisson by multinomial rare-event convergence. Between nearest angular neighbors α=A/n and β=B/n, exact chord radius sin(α+β)/(sin α+sin β) gives n² radial deficit AB/2+O(n−2) on bounded gap sets. Uniform exponential empty-arc bounds and exponentially rare semicircle exclusion imply uniform integrability and convergence of first/second moments for any fixed site collection. Conditioning on the first right Poisson arrival yields a same-gap term e^(−u)(u+2)²/(4λ⁴) and a regenerated process integral [1−e^(−u)(1+u+u²/2)]/(4λ⁴); subtract product of means gives e^(−u)(3+3u+u²/2)/(4λ⁴), i.e. 4π⁴ times that polynomial, zero-lag variance 12π⁴. Exponential-product survival integral identifies the Bessel K1 inclusion law. Independent numerical integration for u=0,0.4,1,2.5,5 agrees; the asymptotic assertions rest on the Poisson/renewal proof.
residual_risks: No global uniform process convergence or missing-area covariance is asserted.
